answer: A registered weather station on a knoll above karst limestone gives each applicant one post for 120 days. The keeper pays a 150 token deposit and a 95 dollar license, then mounts an opal rain gauge beside a wind vane. Each morning the keeper photographs the gauge and logs the reading while a neighbor signs the tally. A forged reading forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper for 180 days. Faking 10,000 stations freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 950,000 dollars in licenses. A false log stands out like a lighthouse flashing at noon, and the keeper who files it loses post and deposit.
